definition: ML.NET is a free software machine learning library for the C# and F# programming languages.
details: It also supports Python models when used together with NimbusML. The preview release of ML.NET included transforms for feature engineering like n-gram creation, and learners to handle binary classification, multi-class classification, and regression tasks. Additional ML tasks like anomaly detection and recommendation systems have since been added, and other approaches like deep learning will be included in future versions.

explainer.lead: ML.NET is a free machine learning library for C# and F#. It matters because it lets .NET developers add and train models inside their existing codebase.

tiers.eli5: It's a toolbox built for a particular language family, so people already writing C# software can add machine learning without switching tools.
tiers.practitioner: Teams use ML.NET to build transforms for feature engineering, such as n-gram creation, and to train binary classification, multi-class classification and regression learners, with anomaly detection and recommendation tasks added later. One pitfall is scope: deep learning was not yet part of the library and was listed only as an intended future addition.
tiers.paperLevel: A machine learning library for C# and F#; it can incorporate Python models when combined with NimbusML. Its stated task coverage is binary classification, multi-class classification, regression, plus later anomaly detection and recommendation systems.

explainer.example: A C# developer builds an n-gram transform over customer text and trains a binary classification learner to label it.
